subject: Civil Engineering
title: Environmental Impacts of Dams
description: A 60-second lesson on Environmental Impacts of Dams.

hook.text: Dams provide power and water — but they devastate river ecosystems and displace communities.

buildup.text: Dams block fish migration — salmon can't reach spawning grounds. Populations collapse.

discovery.text: Reservoirs flood valleys — destroying habitats, farmland, and sometimes entire towns.

twist.text: Downstream rivers lose sediment, nutrients, and natural flood pulses — deltas erode and shrink.

climax.text: Dam removal is growing — the US removed over 2,000 dams to restore rivers.

punchline.text: Every dam is a trade-off — power and water versus ecosystems and communities.

quiz.question: Why does dam removal restore river ecosystems?
options: It allows fish to migrate freely and restores natural sediment and flood cycles
Removing concrete adds nutrients to the river water
It increases water temperature to levels preferred by native fish species

details.summary: Dams fundamentally alter river ecosystems by blocking fish migration, changing downstream flow patterns, trapping sediment and nutrients, flooding terrestrial habitat, and altering water temperature and dissolved oxygen.
details.whyItMatters: Dams have driven freshwater species to decline faster than any other vertebrate group. Balancing human water needs with ecological integrity is one of the greatest environmental challenges of dam management.
takeaways: Dams block fish migration routes critical for species like salmon
Altered flow regimes change downstream habitat and ecosystem function
Reservoir flooding permanently destroys terrestrial and riparian ecosystems

faq.question: How do fish passage systems help mitigate dam impacts on aquatic species?
faq.answer: Fish ladders provide a series of stepped pools that fish can jump through to pass over the dam. Fish lifts or elevators transport fish in water-filled chambers. Bypass channels route fish around the dam structure.

faq.question: What are environmental flows and why are they important?
faq.answer: Environmental flows are controlled water releases from dams that mimic natural river flow patterns to sustain downstream ecosystems. They include base flows for habitat maintenance, pulse flows that trigger fish spawning and floodplain inundation, and flood flows that transport sediment.
